newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-WELSH CLUBS THRIVE ON EUROPEAN STAGE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WELSH CLUBS THRIVE ON EUROPEAN STAGE.

text.p: Cardiff and Pontypridd boosted the profile of Welsh club rugby on Wednesday as they protected their 100 per cent European Cup records at the expense of Irish and Scottish provincial opposition.

Cardiff produced their second fine display in four days to defeat Munster 48-18 with internationals Rob Howley and Emyr Lewis scoring a hat-trick of tries apiece, putting them top of the competitive pool D which also includes Toulouse and Wasps.
Pontypridd continued to fly the Welsh flag in pool A with a 32-10 win over Edinburgh, building on their success over Milan last weekend helped by three tries by replacement Simon Enoch.

But Cardiff now face a daunting trip this weekend to play defending champions Toulouse, who made an impressive start to the defence of their title in front of a desultory crowd of less than 700 in pouring rain in Milan.
Toulouse won 44-26 against a Milan side coached by former French international Jean Trillo but missing the Cuttitta brothers and two other injured first-teamers.
Milan were kept in the match for most of the first-half by Italy and former Pumas fly-half Diego Dominguez who kicked four penalties in reply to two Toulouse tries.

But a pushover try in the 37th minute, converted by Thomas Castaignede, and a 40th minute try by Christophe Deylaud put Toulouse 29-12 ahead at the interval and two second-half tries were not enough to save Milan from a second defeat in two matches.
Scottish Borders bounced back from their 85-28 weekend hammering by Pau to defeat Llanelli 24-16 with eight penalties from former professional soccer player Gary Parker.
The result allowed Leicester to move into second place in pool B with a 27-10 win in their opening match against Leinster in Dublin.
Former England captain Will Carling kicked 11 points but looked ill at ease in his new club role at fly-half as Harlequins scraped past Ulster 21-15 in Belfast.
